codeReview: Primary selection is now a direct action with a top-to-bottom instruction and explicit return destination.
Source completion delegates through the owning controller; cancellation and source closure cannot reopen setup.
Recognition completion is consumed synchronously from the publisher value while the setup is covered.
Completion is disabled in the UI and guarded in the controller while OCR is pending.
The existing setup host remains alive across the source/Auto round trip; zero-pick sessions preserve established rows.
limits: Activation-prohibited process intentionally cannot become the user's active app. An in-process recorder intercepts and forwards the actual production makeKeyAndOrderFront calls to verify their target; this checks focus requests, not OS-level key-window status.
Real printed labels are recognized through the production document OCR entry point; the harness does not synthesize PDF mouse-coordinate selection gestures, whose implementation is unchanged.
No detector, crop quality, export or corpus-completeness claim follows from these UI checks.
reproduce: bash tools/test_instrument_pick_flow.sh (macOS with native AppKit/Vision rendering access; no App main or user documents)

visualReview.captureLimit: NSView cache-display captures in an inactive activation-prohibited process omit prominent button bezel fills. These are layout/label checks, not a certification of active-window color contrast.
observations: Empty setup at 800 by 580 points keeps the selection instruction and primary action in the visible setup area; descriptive text wraps.
Source at 760 by 650 points retains a fixed bottom instruction/action area outside the PDF viewport, with selected-label chip and count.
The populated setup shows both distinct numbered violins in source order and the next instruction to review and choose Auto.

Review found a green highlight spilling into the instruction header when its label was scrolled outside the PDF viewport. The final clipped editor group stops that spill; the final source-selecting image shows a clean header.
